en: Itivuttaka 5: Ekakanipāta, First Chapter Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. What is that one thing? Greed (*lobha*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, the venerable Ānanda addressed the monks: "Friends, monks! "Yes, friend," those monks replied to the venerable Ānanda. The venerable Ānanda said this: "Friends, the Blessed One spoke this brief statement in the presence of the monks: 'Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. What is that one thing? Greed. This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. Now, friends, what is the meaning of this brief statement spoken by the Blessed One? When this was said, the venerable Sāriputta replied to the venerable Ānanda: "Friend Ānanda, greed is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. Why is that? Because, friend, when greed has arisen in a person, he destroys himself by means of body, speech, and mind;

and having destroyed himself, he causes others to do so as well; and having caused others to do so, he experiences mental pain and dejection. Thus, friend, greed is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the venerable Sāriputta: "Excellent, friend Sāriputta! Excellent, friend Sāriputta! ... [as in the standard formula] ... Those who have not heard this Dharma and Discipline would have been confused by what was well explained by the venerable Sāriputta. Therefore, friend Sāriputta, remember this Dharma discourse as the *Ekadhamma Sutta* (The Discourse on the One Thing). "Yes, friend," the venerable Sāriputta replied to the venerable Ānanda. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. What is that one thing? Non-greed (*alobha*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting non-greed for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. What is that one thing? Anger (*kodha*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting anger for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. What is that one thing? Non-anger (*akodha*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting non-anger for anger. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. What is that one thing? Delusion (*moha*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting delusion for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. What is that one thing? Non-delusion (*amoha*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting non-delusion for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. What is that one thing? False view (*micchādiṭṭhi*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting false view for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. What is that one thing? Right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting right view for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. What is that one thing? Wrong conduct (*duccarita*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting wrong conduct for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. What is that one thing? Good conduct (*sucarita*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting good conduct for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. What is that one thing? Lack of shame (*ahirika*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting lack of shame for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. What is that one thing? Shame (*hiri*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting shame for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. What is that one thing? Lack of fear of wrongdoing (*anottappa*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting lack of fear of wrongdoing for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. What is that one thing? Fear of wrongdoing (*ottappa*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his welfare and happiness for a long time. [The rest of the sutta follows the same structure as above, substituting fear of wrongdoing for greed. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: "Monks, there is this one thing which, when it arises in a person, leads to his harm and suffering for a long time. What is that one thing? Sloth and torpor
Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard:
I am your guarantor for non-returning.
Monks, abandon this one thing: disparagement.
This is what the Blessed One said.
With reference to this, it is said:
“Having fully understood that flattery by which beings go to an evil destination—
that flattery, having rightly known it...”
Those who possess insight abandon them;
having abandoned them, they never again return to this world.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
